# Portfolio Data and Rate Limits Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking. This
> session executes the plan inline rather than dispatching subagents, because the
> operator's standing instruction forbids the Agent tool unless asked for.

**Goal:** Serve the portfolio section from a committed `projects.json` generated by a
hand-run script, so a visitor never calls the GitHub API, dead demo links never render,
and the filter reads a GitHub topic instead of a magic word in the description.

**Architecture:** `tools/build_projects.py` fetches the two accounts, keeps repos
carrying the `portfolio` topic that are not archived, probes each `homepage` and drops
the ones that do not answer, and writes `projects.json`. The renderer in `index.html`
drops its three GitHub API calls for one same-origin `fetch('/projects.json')`. The
~300 lines of CSS the renderer injected at runtime move into `css/style.css`. A sixth
verifier, `tools/verify_portfolio.py`, pins the issue's acceptance criteria the way the
other five pin theirs.

**Tech Stack:** Vanilla JS (no build step), Python 3 standard library only, GitHub REST
v3 via `urllib.request`.

**Spec:** GitHub issue #20, "Portfolio section: GitHub API rate limits, fragile
filtering, and dead demo links". Four scope decisions were taken by the site owner on
2026-08-13 and are recorded in "Owner decisions" below.

## Global Constraints

- **Standard library only** in `tools/`. No pip dependency, no build step, no CI. The
  five existing verifiers and the two image scripts all hold this line.
- **No emoji and no em dashes** in any file, commit, or PR text. Global operator rule.
- **JavaScript, never TypeScript.** Global operator rule.
- **Every verifier globs `*.html` at the repo root** rather than naming pages, so a page
  added later is covered instead of silently exempt.
- **Verifiers strip comments before any regex scan**, because a comment has to quote the
  thing it explains and a bare substring scan counts that explanation as the offense.
- **`safeUrl()` stays in the renderer.** It accepts `https:` and returns `null` for
  anything else, and a `null` means the link does not render at all.
- **The renderer builds DOM nodes and sets `textContent`.** No template literal reaches
  `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, or `insertAdjacentHTML` with an interpolation in it.
- **Run all six verifiers before opening the PR**, from the repository root.

## Owner decisions

| Question | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Freshness mechanism | Hand-run `tools/build_projects.py`, no GitHub Action, no cron |
| Editing the GitHub repos | Authorized: add the `portfolio` topic, strip `#portfolio` from descriptions |
| Dead demo links | Generator probes each URL and silently omits a demo that does not answer |
| Project set | Drop the `MapTheVoteSTL` account; drop the two archived CleanUpCoop forks |

Not chosen, and therefore not built: adding `CleanUpCoop` to the portfolio, and a
`featured` topic for manual ordering. Sorting stays `updated_at` descending.

Seven projects ship. `Seaside-Sustainability-Web-GIS` stays in `ACCOUNTS` and contributes

## Already fixed, do not re-fix

The issue was filed against an older `index.html`. Two of its findings no longer apply:

- **Finding 8's stray formatting bug.** `background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.7);    opacity: 0;`
  is already two properties on two lines at `index.html:910-911`.
- **Finding 9's emoji in the error output.** `index.html:735-737` is plain text. The only
  emoji-range codepoint left in `index.html` is the `★` at line 670, which Task 4 removes.

`resume.html` carries six emoji-range codepoints at lines 368, 460, and 466: the moon and
sun glyphs on its dark mode toggle. Those are visible UI on a page this issue does not
mention, so they stay, and `verify_portfolio.py` scopes its emoji scan to `index.html`
and says why in its docstring.

## File Structure

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `tools/verify_portfolio.py` (new) | Pins issue 20's seven acceptance criteria. Pure functions from the generator are unit-tested here with injected fetchers and probes, so the gate stays offline and deterministic. `--check-links` opts into a live probe. |
| `tools/build_projects.py` (new) | Fetches, filters, probes, writes `projects.json`. Every decision lives in a pure function that takes its I/O as a parameter. |
| `projects.json` (new, committed) | The generated data the page reads. |
| `index.html` (modify) | Renderer reads `/projects.json`. Loses the `githubUsers` list, the three-account loop, and the 300-line CSS string. Gains a star icon, `aria-hidden` on its three decorative icons, and `.portfolio-error` in place of an inline style. |
| `css/style.css` (modify) | Receives the portfolio CSS verbatim, plus `.portfolio-error`. |
| `tools/verify_seo_a11y.py` (modify) | `check_text_contrast` reads `css/style.css` instead of `index.html`; `.portfolio-error` joins `CONTRAST_PAIRS`. |
| `tools/verify_security.py` (modify) | `remote_fields` renamed to the fields that now exist, so the interpolation check keeps its teeth instead of asserting nothing. |
| `tools/verify_assets.py` (modify) | `projects.json` joins `HOMEPAGE_ASSETS`; it is now a first-paint fetch. |

**The renderer's loop variable stays named `repo`.** Three checks in
`verify_security.py` are pinned to the literal text `repo.` at a sink
(`window.open(repo.`, `href = repo.`, `setAttribute('href', repo.`). Renaming the
variable to `project` would leave all three matching nothing and passing vacuously,
which is the exact failure mode this repo keeps writing verifiers to prevent.

## projects.json schema

```json
{
  "generated": "2026-08-13T00:00:00Z",
  "projects": [
    {
      "name": "QuakeGlobe",
      "description": "QuakeGlobe is a real-time 3D earthquake visualizer ...",
      "language": "TypeScript",
      "stars": 0,
      "code": "https://github.com/GeoBradDev/QuakeGlobe",
      "demo": "https://quakeglobe.onrender.com/",
      "updated": "2025-05-24T17:37:08Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

`demo` is `null` when the repo has no homepage, when the homepage is not `https:`, or
when the probe did not answer. `description` and `language` are `""` rather than `null`
when GitHub supplies nothing, so the renderer's `||` fallbacks stay simple. `generated`
exists because staleness is the one real cost of the hand-run choice, and a reader
should be able to see how stale the file is without checking git.

### Task 1: Pin the acceptance criteria in a sixth verifier

**Files:**
- Create: `tools/verify_portfolio.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: nothing yet. Task 3 creates the module this imports, so every check that
  imports `build_projects` fails until then. That is the RED step.
- Produces: `python3 tools/verify_portfolio.py`, exit 0 or 1, and a `--check-links` flag.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the verifier**

Header and constants, matching the five existing verifiers' shape:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check the portfolio data criteria from issue 20.

Run from the repository root:

    python3 tools/verify_portfolio.py

Exits 0 when every criterion holds, 1 otherwise. Standard library only, so it
runs anywhere Python 3 does and adds no build step to the site.

Offline and deterministic by default, like the other five. The one criterion
that cannot be settled from the source, "every Live Demo link resolves", is
settled two ways: the generator probes every homepage at generation time and
omits the ones that do not answer, and this file unit-tests that probing logic
with an injected probe. Pass --check-links to additionally probe the URLs that
actually shipped in projects.json, which needs the network and is therefore not
part of the default gate.

The emoji scan below covers index.html alone. resume.html carries a moon and a
sun glyph on its dark mode toggle at lines 368, 460, and 466. Those are visible
UI on a page issue 20 does not mention, and removing them is a design change
this issue did not ask for.
"""

import json
import re
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
INDEX = ROOT / "index.html"
STYLE_CSS = ROOT / "css" / "style.css"
PROJECTS = ROOT / "projects.json"

sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools"))

# Codepoint ranges that carry pictographs, written as escapes rather than as
# literal characters: a range whose endpoints are invisible glyphs is a range
# nobody can review, and U+FE0F in particular is zero-width. U+2605 BLACK STAR
# sits in Miscellaneous Symbols and is caught by the first range, which is the
# point: it was the last non-ASCII character in index.html.
EMOJI_RANGES = re.compile(
    "[\u2600-\u27bf\u2b00-\u2bff\ufe0f\U0001f000-\U0001faff]"
)

# Selectors the portfolio cards need. Asserting the CSS moved means asserting
# it arrived, not just that it left index.html.
MOVED_SELECTORS = [
    "#github-projects",
    ".portfolio-item",
    ".portfolio-card",
    ".portfolio-title",
    ".portfolio-description p",
    ".portfolio-stars",
    ".portfolio-language",
    ".portfolio-link-demo",
    ".portfolio-link-code",
    ".portfolio-overlay",
    ".portfolio-error",
]

PROBE_TIMEOUT = 15

failures = []


def fail(message):
    failures.append(message)
    print("  FAIL  " + message)


def check(condition, message):
    if condition:
        print("  PASS  " + message)
    else:
        fail(message)
    return condition


def read(path):
    """Return path's text, or None if the file does not exist.

    Same contract as verify_security.read: a missing file becomes one FAIL
    line from the caller instead of a traceback that kills every remaining
    check partway through the run.
    """
    if not path.exists():
        return None
    return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")


def read_or_fail(path):
    text = read(path)
    check(text is not None, "%s exists" % path.relative_to(ROOT))
    return text


def without_comments(source, style):
    """Strip comments so a scan reads code, not prose about code.

    Same helper, and the same reason, as verify_assets.without_comments: a
    comment has to quote the thing it explains, and the comment in index.html
    saying why the renderer no longer calls api.github.com contains the string
    "api.github.com".
    """
    pattern = r"/\*.*?\*/" if style == "css" else r"<!--.*?-->"
    return re.sub(pattern, "", source, flags=re.S)
```

The checks. Each one names the acceptance criterion it pins:

```python
def check_no_visitor_side_api_call():
    """Criterion 1. The section renders with no GitHub API call from a visitor."""
    print("\nThe page makes no GitHub API call")

    source = read_or_fail(INDEX)
    if source is None:
        return
    source = without_comments(source, "html")

    check(
        "api.github.com" not in source,
        "index.html does not call api.github.com",
    )
    check(
        "projects.json" in source,
        "index.html reads the generated projects.json instead",
    )


def check_projects_json_is_well_formed():
    """Criteria 1 and 5. The committed data is complete and every URL is https."""
    print("\nprojects.json is well formed")

    raw = read_or_fail(PROJECTS)
    if raw is None:
        return

    try:
        data = json.loads(raw)
    except ValueError as error:
        fail("projects.json is not valid JSON: %s" % error)
        return
    check(True, "projects.json parses")

    if not check(isinstance(data, dict), "projects.json holds an object"):
        return
    check(
        isinstance(data.get("generated"), str) and data["generated"].endswith("Z"),
        "projects.json records a UTC generation timestamp",
    )

    projects = data.get("projects")
    if not check(isinstance(projects, list), "projects.json holds a projects list"):
        return
    if not check(bool(projects), "projects.json is not empty"):
        return

    for index, project in enumerate(projects):
        label = "project %d" % index
        if not check(isinstance(project, dict), "%s is an object" % label):
            continue
        label = project.get("name") or label

        check(
            isinstance(project.get("name"), str) and project["name"].strip() != "",
            "%s names a repo" % label,
        )
        for field in ("description", "language"):
            check(
                isinstance(project.get(field), str),
                "%s has a string %s, never null" % (label, field),
            )
        check(
            isinstance(project.get("stars"), int) and project["stars"] >= 0,
            "%s has a non-negative star count" % label,
        )
        code = project.get("code")
        check(
            isinstance(code, str) and code.startswith("https://"),
            "%s links its code over https" % label,
        )
        demo = project.get("demo")
        check(
            demo is None or (isinstance(demo, str) and demo.startswith("https://")),
            "%s demo link is https or absent, never anything else" % label,
        )


def check_no_magic_word_in_descriptions():
    """Criterion 3. The control flag is out of the user-facing copy."""
    print("\nNo control flag leaks into a description")

    raw = read(PROJECTS)
    if raw is None:
        return
    try:
        projects = json.loads(raw).get("projects", [])
    except ValueError:
        return

    # The flag was written as a trailing hashtag, "#portfolio". A description
    # may still use the ordinary word: "a portfolio of neighborhood maps" is
    # prose, not a control flag, and failing on it would push the copy around
    # to satisfy a checker.
    for project in projects:
        description = project.get("description", "")
        check(
            "#portfolio" not in description.lower(),
            "%s description carries no #portfolio flag" % project.get("name", "?"),
        )


def check_filter_reads_topics_not_descriptions():
    """Criterion 3, at the generator. Filtering is topic-based, proven by behavior."""
    print("\nThe generator filters on the portfolio topic")

    try:
        import build_projects
    except ImportError as error:
        fail("tools/build_projects.py is importable: %s" % error)
        return

    tagged = {"name": "tagged", "topics": ["portfolio"], "archived": False,
              "description": "no flag here"}
    described = {"name": "described", "topics": [], "archived": False,
                 "description": "matches the old filter #portfolio"}
    archived = {"name": "archived", "topics": ["portfolio"], "archived": True,
                "description": ""}
    untopiced = {"name": "untopiced", "archived": False, "description": ""}

    selected = [r["name"] for r in
                build_projects.select_repos([tagged, described, archived, untopiced])]

    check("tagged" in selected, "a repo with the portfolio topic is selected")
    check(
        "described" not in selected,
        "a repo with the word in its description but no topic is rejected",
    )
    check("archived" not in selected, "an archived repo is rejected")
    check(
        "untopiced" not in selected,
        "a repo with no topics key at all is rejected without raising",
    )


def check_one_account_failure_does_not_blank_the_section():
    """Criterion 2. A failing account costs its own repos and nothing else."""
    print("\nOne failing account does not blank the section")

    try:
        import build_projects
    except ImportError as error:
        fail("tools/build_projects.py is importable: %s" % error)
        return

    def fetcher(account):
        if account == "broken":
            raise RuntimeError("simulated 502")
        return [{"name": account + "-repo", "topics": ["portfolio"],
                 "archived": False, "description": ""}]

    repos, failed = build_projects.collect(["broken", "working"], fetcher)
    check(
        [r["name"] for r in repos] == ["working-repo"],
        "a working account still contributes when another one fails",
    )
    check(failed == ["broken"], "the failing account is reported by name")

    # Every account failing is a different situation: there is no partial
    # result to keep, and writing an empty projects.json would blank the
    # section far more thoroughly than the bug this criterion is about.
    try:
        build_projects.collect(["broken"], fetcher)
    except RuntimeError:
        check(True, "every account failing raises instead of returning nothing")
    else:
        fail("every account failing raises instead of returning nothing")


def check_dead_demo_links_are_dropped():
    """Criterion 5. A demo that does not answer never reaches the page."""
    print("\nA dead demo link is dropped at generation time")

    try:
        import build_projects
    except ImportError as error:
        fail("tools/build_projects.py is importable: %s" % error)
        return

    live = build_projects.resolve_demo("https://example.com/", lambda url: True)
    dead = build_projects.resolve_demo("https://example.com/", lambda url: False)
    insecure = build_projects.resolve_demo("http://example.com/", lambda url: True)
    missing = build_projects.resolve_demo(None, lambda url: True)

    check(live == "https://example.com/", "a demo that answers is kept")
    check(dead is None, "a demo that does not answer is dropped")
    check(insecure is None, "a non-https homepage is dropped without probing")
    check(missing is None, "a repo with no homepage yields no demo link")


def check_portfolio_css_lives_in_the_stylesheet():
    """Criterion 6. The CSS is a stylesheet, not a string injected at runtime."""
    print("\nPortfolio CSS lives in css/style.css")

    markup = read_or_fail(INDEX)
    css = read_or_fail(STYLE_CSS)
    if markup is None or css is None:
        return
    markup = without_comments(markup, "html")

    check(
        "portfolioCSS" not in markup,
        "index.html no longer builds a CSS string in JavaScript",
    )
    check(
        "insertAdjacentHTML" not in markup,
        "index.html no longer injects markup at runtime",
    )
    for selector in MOVED_SELECTORS:
        check(
            re.search(r"(?m)^%s\s*\{" % re.escape(selector), css) is not None,
            "css/style.css styles %s" % selector,
        )


def check_no_emoji_in_the_homepage():
    """Criterion 7. No pictograph in any output the page produces."""
    print("\nNo emoji in index.html")

    source = read_or_fail(INDEX)
    if source is None:
        return

    hits = sorted(set(EMOJI_RANGES.findall(source)))
    check(
        not hits,
        "index.html carries no emoji or pictograph (found %s)"
        % (", ".join("U+%04X" % ord(c) for c in hits) or "none"),
    )

    raw = read(PROJECTS)
    if raw is None:
        return
    hits = sorted(set(EMOJI_RANGES.findall(raw)))
    check(
        not hits,
        "projects.json carries no emoji or pictograph (found %s)"
        % (", ".join("U+%04X" % ord(c) for c in hits) or "none"),
    )


def check_links_live():
    """Opt-in, network. Probe the demo URLs that actually shipped."""
    print("\nEvery shipped demo link answers (live probe)")

    raw = read(PROJECTS)
    if raw is None:
        return
    try:
        projects = json.loads(raw).get("projects", [])
    except ValueError:
        return

    probed = 0
    for project in projects:
        demo = project.get("demo")
        if not demo:
            continue
        probed += 1
        request = urllib.request.Request(demo, method="GET",
                                         headers={"User-Agent": "verify_portfolio"})
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=PROBE_TIMEOUT) as response:
                status = response.status
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
            status = error.code
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - any failure is a dead link
            fail("%s demo %s did not answer: %s" % (project.get("name"), demo, error))
            continue
        check(status < 400, "%s demo answers %d" % (project.get("name"), status))

    if probed == 0:
        print("  skip  no project ships a demo link")


def main():
    check_no_visitor_side_api_call()
    check_projects_json_is_well_formed()
    check_no_magic_word_in_descriptions()
    check_filter_reads_topics_not_descriptions()
    check_one_account_failure_does_not_blank_the_section()
    check_dead_demo_links_are_dropped()
    check_portfolio_css_lives_in_the_stylesheet()
    check_no_emoji_in_the_homepage()
    if "--check-links" in sys.argv:
        check_links_live()

    print()
    if failures:
        print("%d check(s) failed." % len(failures))
        return 1
    print("All checks passed.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

### Task 2: Set the GitHub topics and strip the magic word

**Files:** none in the repository. This task changes external state on GitHub, which is
why it comes before the generator: the generator reads that state.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: nothing.
- Produces: three repos gain the `portfolio` topic; seven descriptions lose their
  trailing `#portfolio`. Task 3's generated `projects.json` depends on both.

- [ ] **Step 1: Record the before state**

```bash
gh api "users/GeoBradDev/repos?per_page=100" \
  --jq '.[] | select((.topics | index("portfolio")) or ((.description // "") | test("#portfolio"))) | "\(.name) topics=\(.topics) desc=\(.description)"'
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Add the topic to the three repos missing it**

The topics endpoint replaces the whole list, so each call has to send the existing
topics plus `portfolio`. All three currently have none, verified in Step 1.

```bash
for repo in STLTaxAuctionGeoprocessing WebGIS-React-Native St-Louis-Neighborhood-Atlas; do
  gh api -X PUT "repos/GeoBradDev/$repo/topics" -f "names[]=portfolio"
done
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Strip the trailing flag from the seven non-archived descriptions**

Read each description, remove the trailing `#portfolio` and the whitespace before it,
and PATCH it back. Never hand-retype a description: they are long and a typo is silent.

```bash
for repo in STLTaxAuctionGeoprocessing WebGIS-Django WebGIS-React WebGIS-React-Native \
            WWJC_ChromeExtension St-Louis-Neighborhood-Atlas QuakeGlobe; do
  desc=$(gh api "repos/GeoBradDev/$repo" --jq '.description' \
         | sed -E 's/[[:space:]]*#portfolio[[:space:]]*$//')
  gh api -X PATCH "repos/GeoBradDev/$repo" -f description="$desc"
done
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Verify the after state**

```bash
gh api "users/GeoBradDev/repos?per_page=100" \
  --jq '.[] | select(.topics | index("portfolio")) | "\(.name) | topics=\(.topics) | flag=\((.description // "") | test("#portfolio"))"'
```

Expected: seven rows, every `topics` containing `portfolio`, every `flag` `false`.

The two archived CleanUpCoop forks are deliberately untouched. GitHub rejects a write to
an archived repository, and both the archived filter and the topic filter exclude them,
so their descriptions keep a flag that nothing reads.

Nothing in the working tree changed. The next task's `projects.json` is where this

### Task 3: Write the generator and generate the data

**Files:**
- Create: `tools/build_projects.py`
- Create: `projects.json`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: the topics set in Task 2.
- Produces, all imported by name from `tools/verify_portfolio.py`:
  - `select_repos(repos) -> list[dict]`
  - `collect(accounts, fetch_repos) -> tuple[list[dict], list[str]]`, raising
    `RuntimeError` when every account fails
  - `resolve_demo(homepage, probe) -> str | None`
  - `https_url(value) -> str | None`
  - `to_project(repo, demo) -> dict`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the generator**

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate projects.json for the portfolio section (issue 20).

Run from anywhere:

    python3 tools/build_projects.py

Writes projects.json at the repository root. Standard library only, and run by
hand like tools/optimize_images.py and tools/make_og_card.py rather than as
part of a build: this site has no build step, and the data changes about as
often as the repos do.

Why a generated file at all. The renderer used to call the GitHub API three
times per page load, once per account. The unauthenticated limit is 60 requests
per hour per IP address, which is roughly 20 page loads from a shared address
before the section shows an error instead of any work. A committed file makes
that failure mode structurally impossible: a visitor fetches one same-origin
static file and never talks to GitHub.

Set GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN to raise this script's own rate limit. It is
optional: three requests fits inside the unauthenticated limit comfortably.

Re-run this after adding the portfolio topic to a repo, after editing a
description, or after redeploying a demo that had gone dark.
"""

import json
import os
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUTPUT = ROOT / "projects.json"

# MapTheVoteSTL was removed on 2026-08-13 (issue 20, criterion 4). Its one
# repo has no description and no topic, so it could never contribute a card.
#
# Seaside-Sustainability-Web-GIS stays even though it contributes nothing
# today: both of its matching repos are archived forks and are filtered out.
# With no visitor-side API call, an account that matches nothing costs nothing,
# and leaving it configured means a future repo there appears without a code
# change.
ACCOUNTS = [
    "GeoBradDev",
    "Seaside-Sustainability-Web-GIS",
]

# GitHub topics are the intended mechanism for this. The old filter looked for
# the word "portfolio" in the description, which put a control flag in copy a
# visitor to the repo reads, and broke silently whenever a description got
# reworded.
PORTFOLIO_TOPIC = "portfolio"

API = "https://api.github.com/users/%s/repos?per_page=100&sort=updated"
USER_AGENT = "geobrad.dev-build-projects"
FETCH_TIMEOUT = 30
PROBE_TIMEOUT = 15


def https_url(value):
    """The URL if it parses and is https, else None.

    Mirrors safeUrl() in index.html on purpose. The renderer validates again at
    render time, because a hand-edited projects.json is still untrusted input;
    this half keeps a javascript: or http: homepage from ever being written to
    the file in the first place.
    """
    if not isinstance(value, str) or value == "":
        return None
    try:
        parsed = urllib.parse.urlparse(value)
    except ValueError:
        return None
    if parsed.scheme != "https" or not parsed.netloc:
        return None
    return value


def select_repos(repos):
    """Repos carrying the portfolio topic that are not archived.

    Archived is excluded because an archived repo is frozen: its demo is
    usually gone, its description cannot be edited to fix a flag, and it is
    weaker portfolio material than anything still moving.
    """
    selected = []
    for repo in repos:
        topics = repo.get("topics") or []
        if PORTFOLIO_TOPIC not in topics:
            continue
        if repo.get("archived"):
            continue
        selected.append(repo)
    return selected


def collect(accounts, fetch_repos):
    """Every account's repos, tolerating a failure in any one of them.

    Returns (repos, failed_accounts). One account being rate limited, renamed,
    or 502ing used to throw and leave the whole section blank; now it costs
    only its own repos.

    Every account failing is a different situation and raises: there is no
    partial result to keep, and writing an empty projects.json would blank the
    section far more thoroughly than the bug this guards against.
    """
    repos = []
    failed = []
    for account in accounts:
        try:
            repos.extend(fetch_repos(account))
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - one bad account is not fatal
            failed.append(account)
            print("  WARN  %s failed: %s" % (account, error), file=sys.stderr)
    if failed and len(failed) == len(accounts):
        raise RuntimeError("every account failed; refusing to write an empty file")
    return repos, failed


def resolve_demo(homepage, probe):
    """The homepage if it is https and answers, else None.

    Six of the nine repos this section used to show pointed at Render's free
    tier, and four of those had 404'd outright by 2026-08-13. A Live Demo link
    to a dead page is worse than no link, so a URL that does not answer here
    never reaches projects.json and the card renders with a Code link alone.
    """
    url = https_url(homepage)
    if url is None:
        return None
    return url if probe(url) else None


def to_project(repo, demo):
    """One repo as the record the renderer consumes.

    description and language are "" rather than null when GitHub supplies
    nothing, so the renderer's `||` fallbacks stay simple and the schema has
    one nullable field instead of three.
    """
    return {
        "name": repo.get("name") or "",
        "description": repo.get("description") or "",
        "language": repo.get("language") or "",
        "stars": int(repo.get("stargazers_count") or 0),
        "code": https_url(repo.get("html_url")),
        "demo": demo,
        "updated": repo.get("updated_at") or "",
    }


def request(url, timeout):
    headers = {"User-Agent": USER_AGENT, "Accept": "application/vnd.github+json"}
    token = os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN") or os.environ.get("GH_TOKEN")
    if token:
        headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer " + token
    return urllib.request.Request(url, headers=headers)


def fetch_repos(account):
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request(API % account, FETCH_TIMEOUT),
                                timeout=FETCH_TIMEOUT) as response:
        data = json.loads(response.read().decode("utf-8"))
    if not isinstance(data, list):
        raise RuntimeError("expected a list of repos, got %r" % type(data).__name__)
    return data


def probe(url):
    """True when the URL answers below 400.

    GET rather than HEAD: enough hosts answer HEAD with 405 that a HEAD probe
    would drop demos that are perfectly alive.
    """
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request(url, PROBE_TIMEOUT),
                                    timeout=PROBE_TIMEOUT) as response:
            return response.status < 400
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        return error.code < 400
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - anything else is a link a visitor cannot use
        return False


def main():
    repos, failed = collect(ACCOUNTS, fetch_repos)
    for account in ACCOUNTS:
        if account in failed:
            continue
        count = len(select_repos([r for r in repos
                                  if (r.get("owner") or {}).get("login") == account]))
        print("  %-32s %d project(s)" % (account, count))

    selected = sorted(select_repos(repos),
                      key=lambda r: r.get("updated_at") or "", reverse=True)
    if not selected:
        print("No repo carries the %r topic. Refusing to write an empty file."
              % PORTFOLIO_TOPIC, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    projects = []
    for repo in selected:
        demo = resolve_demo(repo.get("homepage"), probe)
        if repo.get("homepage") and demo is None:
            print("  WARN  %s homepage %s did not answer; shipping without a demo link"
                  % (repo.get("name"), repo.get("homepage")), file=sys.stderr)
        if "#portfolio" in (repo.get("description") or "").lower():
            print("  WARN  %s description still carries the #portfolio flag"
                  % repo.get("name"), file=sys.stderr)
        projects.append(to_project(repo, demo))

    payload = {
        "generated": datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
        "projects": projects,
    }
    OUTPUT.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n",
                      encoding="utf-8")
    print("Wrote %s with %d project(s)." % (OUTPUT.relative_to(ROOT), len(projects)))
    if failed:
        print("  %d account(s) failed and contributed nothing: %s"
              % (len(failed), ", ".join(failed)), file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

Move `index.html:746-1043` verbatim, without the `<style>` and `</style>` lines, to the

```css
/*------------------------------------------------
  Portfolio cards

  Moved out of a JavaScript string in index.html by issue 20. It used to be
  built as ~300 lines of CSS in a template literal and injected into <head>
  with insertAdjacentHTML on every page load, which delayed styling until the
  script ran and kept the browser from caching it separately.

  style.css loads after bootstrap.min.css, and this block is at the end of
```

`style.css` declares no `.portfolio-*` or `#github-projects` rule today, verified with

- [ ] **Step 2: Add the error style**

Append after the moved block. `#b3271b` on `#f8f9fa` computes to 5.9:1, over the 4.5:1
AA threshold that `#e74c3c` missed at 3.4:1:

```css
/* The error the renderer shows when projects.json cannot be read. It was an
   inline style at #e74c3c, which is 3.4:1 on the section background and fails
   AA. A message a visitor cannot read is not a message. */
.portfolio-error {
    color: #b3271b;
    background: #f8f9fa;
    font-size: 16px;
}
```

Declaring `background` explicitly matters: `#portfolio` paints a
`#f8f9fa` to `#e9ecef` gradient, and `verify_seo_a11y.check_text_contrast` can only
measure a color the rule states.

## Verification

Beyond the six verifiers, the runtime half. Source checks cannot show that seven cards
render, that a dead `projects.json` degrades to a readable message, or that the moved CSS
looks identical.

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

**The happy path.** Load `http://127.0.0.1:8000/`, scroll to Portfolio. Expect seven
cards in the order `projects.json` lists them; a `fa fa-star` glyph and a number on each;
`Live Demo` on WWJC_ChromeExtension and QuakeGlobe only; `Code` on all seven. Confirm in
the network panel that the page requests `projects.json` and makes **no** request to
`api.github.com`. Confirm the cards are styled on first paint rather than after the
script runs.

**The failure path.** With the server running, request a page whose `projects.json` is
absent. `git stash push projects.json`, reload, and expect the plain-text
`Couldn't load projects. projects.json returned 404.` in `#b3271b`, the loader hidden,
and the rest of the page unaffected. `git stash pop` afterwards.

**The edge path.** Temporarily write `{"generated":"...","projects":[]}` and confirm the
`No portfolio projects found.` empty state renders inside a `col-xs-12`. Restore.

**Keyboard and screen reader.** Tab through a card: the `Live Demo` and `Code` anchors
must both take focus and show a visible ring, and the star count must announce as a
number followed by "GitHub stars" rather than a bare number.

**Lighthouse**, since the CSS moved and the markup changed:

```bash
npx --yes lighthouse@12 http://127.0.0.1:8000/ --only-categories=accessibility,seo,performance \
  --chrome-flags="--headless"
```

Expect accessibility and SEO to hold at 100 with no failing audits.
